preamble: In Jèrriais, the Norman language of Jersey, /r/ before a front vowel, chiefly between vowels and word-finally after a vowel, developed into the voiced dental fricative [ð], written 'th'. The change happened after the 16th century: Sercquiais, brought to Sark by Jersey settlers, does not have it. It is standard in the literary language and predominant in the western dialects, but the eastern dialects keep [ɾ]. No comparable regular r > ð change has been confirmed in another language, so the shift is rare (the Outer Hebridean Scottish Gaelic realization of slender /ɾʲ/ as [ð] starts from a palatalized rhotic and is not included here).
sources: Wikipedia contributors. Jèrriais: Phonology, Dental fricative. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A8rriais
